findings.location: SPEC.md > Capabilities > CAP-5 (warm container ownership) + Constraints (Job ID ownership)
findings.issue: Container ownership is tied to the label psm.owner-pid, which is the PID of the process that booted the container. --cleanup-orphans deletes anything whose owner PID is dead, and ps-run-layer.py creates one Job ID per invocation. A warm canary that survives between fix-loop iterations has no live owner process between invocations. So the first --cleanup-orphans call, from this session or any other session sharing the daemon, will delete it as an orphan. --stop-job (which SIGTERMs the owning process and then removes `psm.job=<id>`) has no process to signal. The phrase 'removed by --cleanup-orphans after its owner dies' is undefined when the owner is meant to die after every iteration.
findings.implementation_impact: The ownership model in ps-flashlight-run.py (owner-pid probe, job_start, cleanup_orphans, stop-job) cannot hold a warm container as written. Either the warm container gets reaped at random by parallel sessions, or the implementer invents an ad-hoc lease and weakens the anti-kill guarantees.
findings.suggestion: Define an explicit lease model for warm containers: a persistent Job ID reused across iterations, an owner identity that outlives single invocations (e.g. a lease file holding session ID and expiry, or a heartbeat label), what --cleanup-orphans treats as dead (lease expired), and how --stop-job behaves when no process is attached. Also add an idle TTL.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-5 success ('reinstalled module and a DB reset to the post-boot baseline')
findings.issue: A DB reset does not reset the container filesystem. ps-flashlight-run.py installs with `cp -r /ps-module-src /var/www/html/modules/$MOD_NAME`. If the target directory already exists, this copies into a nested `$MOD_NAME/ps-module-src` directory instead of replacing it. Files deleted from source also survive. Overrides written to /override, var/cache (class_index, Symfony container, Smarty compile), opcache, and uploaded or generated assets from the previous iteration all persist. 'Post-boot baseline' is also ambiguous: it could mean before or after module install. Layer 5 snapshots after install.
findings.implementation_impact: Warm iterations can run stale module code or stale caches. Findings can then appear or vanish because of residue rather than the patch, which breaks the stated guarantee that previous-iteration data cannot cause a finding.
findings.suggestion: Specify the full reset contract: when the DB snapshot is taken (pre-install), removal of the module dir before re-copy (rm -rf then cp), clearing var/cache, /override, and opcache (or restarting php-fpm), and a test proving that a file deleted from source is gone after a warm iteration.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-2 + tier-matrix.md tier 2 ('all versions × Firefox') + brownfield.md (per-version file naming)
findings.issue: Evidence is stored per version (`<module>-e2e-<ver>.json`), and ps-run-layer.py's merge_versions_field raises an error when one version appears twice with different content. Tier 2 runs Firefox for versions whose Chromium evidence came from tier 1, and CAP-4 writes partial runs. The spec never says where per-(version, browser) evidence lives or how a Firefox-only or failed-only run combines with existing Chromium or full evidence instead of overwriting it.
findings.implementation_impact: A Firefox-only tier 2 run will overwrite the tier 1 Chromium evidence for that version, so the gate can never assemble both browsers. If the implementer adds per-browser entries under one version key instead, --merge-only fails with the 'different content' conflict.
findings.suggestion: Define the evidence storage unit explicitly, either a per-(version, browser) file or a per-version file with a browser-keyed sub-map plus read-merge rules. Also define how merge_versions_field and --merge-only treat cells written by different runs.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-2 + Constraints ('Release-gate evidence comes only from cold boots with the full scenario set')
findings.issue: Freshness in ps-plan-layers.py is file mtime compared with the newest source mtime, plus the image tag. Evidence produced by a warm container or a failed-only run is written later than the source, so it looks fresh. The spec does not define which fields the evidence must record (boot kind cold/warm, scenario completeness full/partial, per-browser run timestamp) for the planner and the aggregate to reject it. A single file mtime also cannot express that the Chromium entry is older than the Firefox entry.
findings.implementation_impact: Without a defined schema, the planner may reuse warm or partial evidence as gate-grade, which is a silent honesty violation, or each script may invent its own marker and drift apart. The 'ready=false' test in the success signal has no field to assert against.
findings.suggestion: Add a schema section to the evidence contract with per-cell fields, e.g. `boot: cold|warm`, `scenario_set: full|partial`, `scenarios_run`, `run_at`, `tag`, `conclusive`. State that per-cell freshness compares run_at, not file mtime. State that plan and aggregate both reject anything other than cold+full.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal ('A clean release gate boots each version at most once') vs tier-matrix.md tiers 0–2
findings.issue: For a clean module the tier plan boots every version more than once. The canary gets a cold full run at the end of tier 0 and is booted again in tier 2 for Firefox. 1.7.8 and 8.1 are booted in tier 1 for Chromium and again in tier 2 for Firefox. Today, both browsers run in one boot per version with `--jobs 3` in parallel. The tiers are also strictly sequential. So the clean path does more boots and adds two serial barriers, which can make it slower than the status quo, against the Why.
findings.implementation_impact: The success signal cannot be met as literally stated, and the clean-path wall-clock may regress. Implementers have no rule for when skipping a re-boot is allowed.
findings.suggestion: Either restate the success signal as 'tier 2 boots each version at most once' and accept the extra boots with a CAP-6 comparison, or allow tier 1 to run both browsers on non-canary versions when tier 0 is clean so each version boots once. Then add an explicit acceptance criterion comparing the clean-path wall-clock with the current baseline.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-3 (fail-fast) + Assumptions ('in-flight cells finish')
findings.issue: ps-run-layer.py starts versions concurrently with `--jobs` defaulting to 3. Tier 1 has 2 cells and tier 2 has 3 versions, so every cell is already in flight when the first finding arrives and there are no 'unstarted cells' to stop. In-flight cells are allowed to finish. So the success claim that wall-clock is 'close to the failing cell's duration, not the full matrix' does not follow under the default configuration. The spec also does not say whether fail-fast operates inside a cell (stop remaining scenarios or the other browser in a CAP-7 pair) or how a cancel signal reaches separate child processes.
findings.implementation_impact: CAP-3 may be implemented as a no-op under the defaults, or it may be implemented by killing in-flight children, which contradicts the assumption and the orphan-safety rules. The acceptance test is ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: State the cell scheduling model (queue with cap N), define fail-fast at three levels (cross-cell, cross-browser within a boot, cross-scenario within a browser), specify the cancel mechanism between ps-run-layer and its children, and rewrite the success criterion so it holds when jobs < cells, plus a note on the expected no-gain case when jobs >= cells.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-3 success ('reported as not-run')
findings.issue: No representation exists for `not-run`. Unstarted versions in ps-run-layer write no per-version file, and --merge-only drops missing versions. The aggregate today reports 'versi tak ada di hasil e2e'. The spec does not say whether not-run is a new status in the layer JSON, a per-cell entry, or simply absence, nor how headless callers see it in their per-version verdict.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate, plan, and headless return may each treat not-run differently: as absent (rerun), as inconclusive, or as an infra error. Operators may also misread not-run versions as infra failures.
findings.suggestion: Define `not-run` as an explicit per-cell status with a reason (e.g. `fail-fast after <cell>`), written to the layer file. Specify that plan treats it as rerun and the aggregate as inconclusive, and add it to the headless return contract.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-2 + Constraints ('All target versions and both browsers remain mandatory') vs 'configured (version, browser)'
findings.issue: The required browser set has three possible sources: `psm_e2e_browsers` config, the `--browsers` flag, and the interactive scope narrowing in SKILL.md On Activation step 2. The spec says both browsers are mandatory but also says 'any configured (version, browser)'. If config lists only chromium, or the operator narrows on purpose, it is unclear whether ready can ever be true, or whether narrowing is still allowed via `--require`.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers must guess whether the required-cell set comes from config, the flag, or a hard-coded {chromium, firefox}. That choice decides whether the bankwire Chromium-only case reproduces the bug or gets fixed.
findings.suggestion: Name the single source of the required browser set: the config value, which `--browsers` narrowing cannot shrink for the gate. State that narrowing only affects what runs, not what is required, and say how SKILL.md's interactive scope menu interacts with this.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-2 (per-cell conclusiveness)
findings.issue: Today a version's e2e is conclusive when at least one browser ran. Per-browser gaps go to `browser_notes`, and BO conclusiveness depends on a per-engine `bo_authed`. The spec requires 'fresh, conclusive, full-scenario' evidence per (version, browser) but never defines per-cell conclusiveness, e.g. Firefox launched but BO login failed in Firefox only, or one engine hit `launch_error`. brownfield.md flags only the freshness gap, not the conclusiveness gap in ps-aggregate.py e2e_layer.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate's version-level `conclusive` will keep passing a version where Firefox's BO assertions were all inconclusive, so ready can be true without real Firefox BO evidence.
findings.suggestion: Define per-cell conclusiveness: engine launched, module installed, bo_authed when the scenarios need BO, and every scenario in the full set evaluated. Require e2e_layer and compute_ready to evaluate per cell.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-2 + Constraints ('Headless callers keep their per-version verdict contract')
findings.issue: ps-plan-layers.py output (`rerun_matrix` entries of {layer, version}, with `all_reuse` as the gate) has no browser dimension. SKILL.md and run-phases.md tell the model to read `all_reuse` and never union booleans by hand. The spec does not say how the plan output changes to express 'Firefox rerun for 8.1' while the version stays 'fresh' for Chromium, or how callers then invoke a browser-scoped rerun.
findings.implementation_impact: Either the plan schema changes in a way that breaks existing readers, or the per-browser rerun is left for the model to derive by hand, reintroducing the manual-union failure the scripts were built to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Specify the new plan output shape, e.g. rerun_matrix entries gaining `browsers: [...]` and `reason`, with backward-compatible `all_reuse`. Add a mapping from rerun entries to the exact ps-run-layer invocation, e.g. `--versions V --browsers firefox`.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 / tier-matrix.md (who sequences tiers)
findings.issue: The spec never assigns tier sequencing to a component. It does not say whether the planner emits 'next tier', a new orchestrator script runs tiers 0→2, or the model follows prose in SKILL.md / run-phases.md. The skill's own design rule is that gate logic lives in scripts, not model judgment, and 'a tier starts only after the previous tier is clean' is exactly such gate logic.
findings.implementation_impact: Without an owner, tier promotion will likely be written as prose for the model to follow. It is then unenforceable and untestable ('no non-canary cell boots until the canary passes' has nothing to assert against), and headless callers may skip tiers.
findings.suggestion: Assign tier logic to a script: e.g. ps-plan-layers emits `tier`, `next_cells`, and `promotion_ready`, and ps-run-layer refuses non-canary cells unless the canary cell has cold+full clean evidence. Name that script in the companions and in a test.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules ('A failure in tier 1 or tier 2 for version V returns the loop to tier 0, with V as the cell being fixed')
findings.issue: The return path is undefined. It is unclear whether V × Chromium becomes the warm cell, which implies a warm container for a non-canary version, or V × Firefox when the failure is Firefox-only. After fixing V, the patch stales the canary 9.1 evidence, and the spec does not say whether the canary must be re-proven cold before tier 1 resumes or V's cold run is enough. A fix for V can also break 9.1, and the spec does not say how that ordering avoids oscillation.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers will produce inconsistent loops: some re-run the 9.1 canary after every V fix, some skip it. The 'tier 0 clean' precondition for tier 1 becomes ambiguous when V is not the canary.
findings.suggestion: Write the state machine explicitly: the failing cell becomes the 'focus cell' (version and browser), it gets a warm container, and promotion requires cold+full clean on the focus cell and then cold+full on the configured canary before tier 1. Also cover the Firefox-only failure case.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > tier 2 'plus any stale Chromium cell'
findings.issue: Tier 2 starts only after tier 1 is clean, and any source patch stales every cell through mtime. So a stale Chromium cell at tier 2 implies a patch after tier 1, which should send the loop back to tier 0, not into tier 2. The only other way to get a stale Chromium cell is an image-tag bump or config change, and the matrix does not cover it.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers could run a patched module straight into tier 2 with only the stale Chromium cells refreshed, skipping canary and fan-out gating.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the clause or define exactly when it applies (e.g. a tag bump with no source change) and state that any source-mtime staleness at tier 2 resets to tier 0.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-4 (failed-only rerun)
findings.issue: 'Scenarios that failed in a version's latest evidence' is underspecified. It does not say which browser's evidence (the cell is version × browser), whether inconclusive scenarios such as BO assertions after a failed login count as failed, or what happens when the latest evidence is itself a passing partial run (the failed set becomes empty and only smoke runs). It also does not cover a scenario file that was renamed or edited, or a failure in the universal smoke itself.
findings.implementation_impact: Repeated failed-only iterations can quietly lose track of the original failures. After one partial pass, the next iteration runs smoke only and declares the cell converged when the real scenario was never re-checked.
findings.suggestion: Key the failed set per (version, browser) and anchor it to the last full-scenario run, not the latest evidence. Include inconclusive scenarios. Match scenarios by name with a fallback to full when the set cannot be resolved, and record in the evidence which scenario set it was.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 (parallel browsers in one container)
findings.issue: The current code drives browsers in one process with the Playwright sync API, a shared mutable `ctx` dict (bo_authed, screenshot_dir, _shots), and a global progress-phase state (`fl.phase`, `progress_version`). Running engines concurrently needs threads, which sync Playwright does not support across threads without a separate instance per thread, or subprocesses, or async. The spec does not state the concurrency mechanism or how two concurrent `browser:<engine>` phases are logged (interleaved START/ALIVE/SLOW). It also does not say whether two simultaneous BO logins with the same admin account invalidate each other's sessions on 8.x/9.x.
findings.implementation_impact: A naive threaded implementation produces shared-state races in ctx and the progress log, and possible BO session clobbering. That yields false inconclusive or blocking findings, which breaks 'findings identical to a sequential run'.
findings.suggestion: Specify the mechanism (e.g. one subprocess or one Playwright instance per engine, each with its own ctx copy), per-engine progress lines, and per-engine admin credentials or a verified concurrent-session test. Make CAP-7 acceptance depend on resolving the open question on global-config scenarios.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Constraints ('Concurrency ... respects one configurable cap')
findings.issue: The cap has no name, default, unit, or enforcement point. It is unclear whether it counts containers, browser processes, or both. ps-run-layer launches separate child processes per version, while CAP-7 browsers would run inside a child, so one cap spans two process levels. It also does not cover the warm canary container, which occupies the daemon the whole time. The cap is per invocation, but saturation comes from other sessions on the shared daemon, which the cap cannot see.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers will either keep `--jobs` (containers only), so CAP-7 can double load unnoticed, or add a second flag, contradicting 'one cap'. The wait-healthy stalls the constraint is meant to prevent can still happen.
findings.suggestion: Name the cap (config key plus flag), define its unit (e.g. weighted slots: container = 1, extra browser = k), give a default, state that ps-run-layer is the single scheduler, and say whether the warm container counts against it.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-6 (phase durations)
findings.issue: The required phases (`bring-up`, `wait-healthy`, `install`, `browser:<engine>`) omit `pull`, `wait-http`, `warmup-bo`, and `teardown`, which the progress log already emits. warmup-bo and wait-http are boot cost on cold 1.7/8 containers. Leaving them out misattributes boot time, which undermines the stated purpose of seeing 'whether boot or browser driving dominates'. Under CAP-7, browser durations overlap, so a sum of phases no longer equals wall-clock, and the spec does not ask for a cell-level wall-clock.
findings.implementation_impact: The baseline the open question depends on will be skewed and cannot be reconciled with the observed waits.
findings.suggestion: Require every phase that emits START/END, plus a per-version wall-clock and per-tier wall-clock. Mark overlapping phases. Specify whether timings come from in-process timers or the progress log, since the progress log is truncated on every run.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Assumptions ('Tiering applies equally to interactive and headless runs') + Constraints (headless contract)
findings.issue: Headless callers (psm-develop and others) call psm-validate once and expect a per-version verdict. Under tiering with fail-fast, a canary failure leaves the other versions not-run, which changes what callers receive. The callers' handling of inconclusive versus failed is not reviewed. The spec also does not say whether headless runs may create warm containers, and with no operator nobody stops them, which conflicts with headless.md's narrow stop rules.
findings.implementation_impact: Headless callers may treat not-run versions as blocked or as infra failures, or loop forever. Warm containers created headless leak on the shared daemon until some later cleanup.
findings.suggestion: State the headless behavior explicitly: no warm containers in headless mode (or a mandatory --stop-job at return), not-run listed in the return JSON, and a note in headless.md and the caller skills on how to interpret not-run.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Assumptions ('The canary ... is configurable') + Constraints (concurrency cap) + CAP-5
findings.issue: The spec introduces new configuration (canary version and browser, concurrency cap, possibly warm-container TTL) but names no config keys, defaults in resolve-psm-config.py / psm-setup, or CLI flags. SKILL.md requires all settings to flow through the resolver and `--config`.
findings.implementation_impact: Each script may add its own flag with a different name and default. The plan and the run then disagree on which cell is the canary, which breaks the tier gate.
findings.suggestion: List the new keys (e.g. `psm_e2e_canary: 9.1:chromium`, `psm_e2e_concurrency`, `psm_e2e_warm_ttl`), their defaults, the resolver and psm-setup changes, and which scripts consume them.

findings.location: SPEC.md:24-26 (CAP-2); brownfield.md:23-24; tier-matrix.md:9
findings.issue: Per-version e2e evidence is one file per (module, layer, version). The spec does not say where per-browser cell evidence lives, or how a Firefox-only tier-2 run for version V merges with V's existing tier-1 Chromium evidence.
findings.implementation_impact: A tier-2 Firefox run overwrites <module>-e2e-<ver>.json and erases V's Chromium evidence. The release gate then reruns Chromium or loses it.
findings.suggestion: Specify per-cell storage: either <module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.json or a read-merge of a browsers{engine: {...}} map inside the per-version file, with per-engine provenance.

findings.location: SPEC.md:24-26 (CAP-2); brownfield.md:24
findings.issue: Freshness is judged by file mtime against source mtime. Once several browser cells share one file, a later write for one engine refreshes the mtime of older content for another engine.
findings.implementation_impact: Chromium evidence recorded before a patch looks fresh after a post-patch Firefox write, so ready can be true on stale evidence.
findings.suggestion: Store a per-cell run timestamp and source-mtime snapshot (or source hash), and judge freshness per cell, not per file.

findings.location: SPEC.md:22-23 (CAP-1); tier-matrix.md:7-9
findings.issue: 'Clean' is not defined for tier promotion. Nothing says whether an inconclusive cell (boot timeout, skipped_image, install failure, skipped_browser, launch error) counts as clean.
findings.implementation_impact: Either the next tier starts on an untested canary, or tiering stalls forever on an infra failure with no stated recovery.
findings.suggestion: Define clean = conclusive pass with full scenarios. State that inconclusive halts promotion, report the infra cause, and offer retry or a narrowed run.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:3,7-9; SPEC.md:67
findings.issue: The canary browser is configurable, but tier 1 covers only 'other versions × Chromium'. If the canary browser is Firefox, the canary-version × Chromium cell belongs to no tier.
findings.implementation_impact: That cell never runs, so ready stays false permanently. Or the planner invents an unspecified extra run.
findings.suggestion: Define tier 1 as (all versions × all browsers in tier-1 engine set) minus the canary cell, or forbid a non-Chromium canary browser.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:3; SPEC.md:67
findings.issue: The canary is configurable, but nothing says what happens when the configured canary version or browser is outside psm_target_versions / psm_e2e_browsers or outside the operator-narrowed --versions/--browsers.
findings.implementation_impact: Tier 0 tests a cell that is not in the target set, or crashes, and promotion rests on irrelevant evidence.
findings.suggestion: Validate the canary against the effective target set. On a mismatch, fall back to newest target × first browser, or exit 2 with a clear message.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:8-9; SPEC.md:47
findings.issue: Empty tiers are not handled. Examples: one target version (tier 1 empty), or browsers narrowed to Chromium only (tier 2 Firefox empty or absent).
findings.implementation_impact: Promotion logic may wait forever on an empty tier, or treat a narrowed set as release-gate complete.
findings.suggestion: Treat an empty tier as vacuously clean for promotion only. Keep ready=false whenever a configured mandatory browser or version was excluded.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md:14; SPEC.md:22
findings.issue: When a cell fails in tier 2 for a Firefox-specific reason, the loop returns to tier 0, whose cell is canary-version × Chromium. That cell cannot reproduce the failure. (This is the browser dimension, which the version open question does not cover.)
findings.implementation_impact: The canary passes immediately and promotes without the fix being exercised. The loop runs a full cold fan-out each time.
findings.suggestion: On a tier-1/2 failure, the fix-loop cell = the failing (version, browser) until it passes, then resume the canary progression.

findings.location: SPEC.md:27-29 (CAP-3); SPEC.md:68
findings.issue: Fail-fast triggers on a 'conclusive blocking finding'. It does not say whether an inconclusive infra failure in the first cell also stops new cells. With --jobs concurrency, 'first' is also undefined.
findings.implementation_impact: After a boot failure the run either burns the full matrix on a broken daemon or stops inconsistently. Results are nondeterministic across runs.
findings.suggestion: State that infra-inconclusive does not trigger fail-fast (or does, explicitly). Define 'first' as the first finding reported in completion order.

findings.location: SPEC.md:27-29 (CAP-3)
findings.issue: The persistence of not-run cells is unspecified. Nothing says whether a not-run cell writes a per-version file that overwrites a previous evidence file for that cell, or writes nothing.
findings.implementation_impact: Prior gate-grade evidence for an unrelated cell can be clobbered. Or a not-run cell leaves an old file that the planner reuses as fresh.
findings.suggestion: Not-run cells write no evidence file and appear only in the run report and aggregate as not-run. The planner keeps judging the existing file by freshness.

findings.location: SPEC.md:30-32 (CAP-4)
findings.issue: Failed-only rerun has no defined behavior when the latest evidence is missing, inconclusive with no failed scenarios, or itself partial, or when failed scenarios were renamed or deleted since.
findings.implementation_impact: Chained partial reruns shrink the scenario set and hide regressions in previously passing scenarios. A rerun with an empty set may report clean.
findings.suggestion: Derive the failed set only from the latest full-scenario evidence for that cell. If none exists or the set is empty, run full. Drop unknown scenario names with a note.

findings.location: SPEC.md:30-32 (CAP-4)
findings.issue: A failed-only rerun skips scenarios that may set up state for later ones (ordering dependence, BO login via ctx bo_authed, config set by an earlier spec).
findings.implementation_impact: The rerun reports false failures, or false passes from missing preconditions, which misdirects the fix loop.
findings.suggestion: Require specs to declare dependencies, or run failed scenarios plus their declared prerequisites, marking prerequisite results as non-evidence.

findings.location: SPEC.md:30-32 (CAP-4); tier-matrix.md:7
findings.issue: It is unspecified which browser a failed-only rerun uses when the latest evidence for the version has failures in a different engine than the canary browser.
findings.implementation_impact: The rerun drives the wrong engine and reports pass while the actual failing cell stays unexercised.
findings.suggestion: Key the failed set per (version, browser) and rerun on the same engine that failed.

findings.location: SPEC.md:33-35 (CAP-5); run-phases.md:134-144
findings.issue: The warm container outlives the invocation that booted it. --cleanup-orphans removes artifacts whose owner PID is dead, so between iterations the owner is dead by design.
findings.implementation_impact: Another session's --cleanup-orphans deletes the warm canary mid-loop, and the next iteration fails or cold-boots silently.
findings.suggestion: Give the warm container a lease (label psm.keepalive-until or a persistent owner process). Have --cleanup-orphans skip unexpired leases and reap expired ones.

findings.location: SPEC.md:33-35 (CAP-5); run-phases.md:121-127
findings.issue: Each ps-run-layer invocation creates a new Job ID, but the warm container keeps the Job ID of the invocation that booted it. The spec does not say which ID later iterations log under, or which ID --stop-job targets.
findings.implementation_impact: The operator stops the wrong job, or cannot stop the warm container by the ID shown in the current run.
findings.suggestion: Keep a stable warm-container Job ID that is reused and printed by every iteration (e.g. --reuse-job <id>). Log both run ID and container job ID.

findings.location: SPEC.md:33-35 (CAP-5)
findings.issue: There is no health check or fallback for a warm container that died, became unhealthy, lost its DB, or runs a different image tag than the current tag map or config resolves.
findings.implementation_impact: The iteration fails as infra or tests the wrong PrestaShop image, and the evidence is attributed to the wrong provenance.
findings.suggestion: Before each warm iteration, verify the container is running and healthy and that its image tag equals resolve_tag. Otherwise tear it down and cold boot, logging the reason.

findings.location: SPEC.md:33-35 (CAP-5)
findings.issue: The DB reset to the post-boot baseline does not say when the baseline is captured, how it is restored, or what happens if capture or restore fails. Patched source sync into the container and PHP or Symfony cache invalidation are also unspecified.
findings.implementation_impact: Stale opcache or cache, or a failed reset, lets the previous iteration's code or data produce findings, which CAP-5 explicitly forbids.
findings.suggestion: Snapshot the DB right after wait-healthy and before install. Restore it, clear the PS cache, and reset opcache each iteration. A failed restore marks the iteration inconclusive and forces a cold boot.

findings.location: SPEC.md:33-35 (CAP-5); tier-matrix.md:13
findings.issue: The end of the warm-container lifecycle is unspecified: who tears it down at promotion (tier 0's last run must be cold), when the canary cell changes, when the loop is abandoned, or on session exit.
findings.implementation_impact: Idle warm containers accumulate on the shared WSL daemon, holding RAM and ports and causing wait-healthy stalls for tier 1.
findings.suggestion: Tear down the warm container before the cold promotion run and on canary change. Set an idle TTL after which the lease expires and --cleanup-orphans reaps it.

findings.location: SPEC.md:49 (Constraints); SPEC.md:39-41 (CAP-7)
findings.issue: The single concurrency cap has no accounting rule. It does not say whether a slot is a container or a browser, whether an idle warm container counts, or what CAP-7 does when the cap leaves no room for two browsers (e.g. cap=1).
findings.implementation_impact: The cap is either exceeded, saturating the daemon, or CAP-7 deadlocks waiting for a slot.
findings.suggestion: Define cost per container and per browser, and count the warm container. When the remaining cap is below 2, run the version's browsers sequentially and log the fallback.

findings.location: SPEC.md:39-41 (CAP-7); brownfield.md:21
findings.issue: Running browsers in parallel shares per-version state: the ctx dict (bo_authed), the per-version screenshot dir and file names, and console and screenshot rollups. The browser phase has no timeout (phase timeout None), so one hung engine blocks the version indefinitely.
findings.implementation_impact: Engines clobber each other's screenshots or auth state, so findings differ from a sequential run. A hung engine stalls the whole tier.
findings.suggestion: Give each engine its own ctx copy and a screenshot subdir per engine. Add a per-engine phase timeout that marks only that cell inconclusive.

findings.location: SPEC.md:36-38 (CAP-6)
findings.issue: Timing semantics are unspecified for phases that do not occur (warm run: no bring-up or wait-healthy), for phases that timed out or failed, for unlisted phases (pull, wait-http, warmup-bo, teardown), and for overlapping parallel browsers.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate mixes null and 0, double-counts overlapped time, or omits pull, so the boot-vs-browser comparison is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Record {phase: {seconds, outcome}} for every phase. Absent phases are omitted (not 0). Report the per-version wall-clock separately from the per-engine sums.

findings.location: SPEC.md:36-38 (CAP-6); run-phases.md:89
findings.issue: The progress log is truncated at each run, and per-version files are rewritten per tier. The spec does not say which run's timings the aggregate surfaces when a cell's evidence came from tiers or runs other than the latest.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate shows timings from the wrong run, or only the last run, so tier 0 versus gate costs are not visible.
findings.suggestion: Store timings inside each cell's evidence record with the run ID and tier. The aggregate lists timings per cell from the evidence actually used.

findings.location: SPEC.md:51, 70 (headless contract)
findings.issue: Tiering and fail-fast introduce not-run and partial cell states, but the spec does not map them onto the existing headless per-version verdict contract.
findings.implementation_impact: psm-develop and others misread not-run as pass or fail, or break on an unknown field value.
findings.suggestion: Define the mapping explicitly: not-run or partial → per-version verdict 'inconclusive' with a reason. Extend headless.md accordingly.

findings.location: SPEC.md:22-23 (CAP-1); SPEC.md:70
findings.issue: Promotion between tiers has no defined trigger: automatic, operator-confirmed in interactive mode, or caller-driven in headless mode. Headless runs also cannot pull images, so a missing canary image blocks tier 0.
findings.implementation_impact: Interactive runs launch hours-long cold tiers without consent, or headless runs stall at tier 0 with no verdict.
findings.suggestion: State that interactive mode asks before tier 1/2 while headless mode auto-promotes. A missing canary image in headless mode returns blocked with the reason.

findings.location: SPEC.md:50; SPEC.md:33-35
findings.issue: Freshness compares evidence mtime with source mtime. Nothing handles a source patch that lands while a cell is running (now more likely during the warm fix loop).
findings.implementation_impact: Evidence from the pre-patch code gets an mtime later than the patch and is reused as fresh at the gate.
findings.suggestion: Record the source mtime or hash at run start in the evidence. The planner compares that recorded value against the current source.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md tiers 1-2 vs source request and Budi's answer
findings.issue: Source: 'Run 9 + Chrome first; when OK, THEN the other versions AND Firefox', and Budi decided Firefox runs in parallel with Chromium in one boot at the release gate. The matrix inserts an extra Chromium-only fan-out tier (tier 1) before Firefox (tier 2). In the clean path, tier 1 has just made every Chromium cell fresh, so tier 2 runs Firefox alone and the 'parallel with Chromium' decision only fires for stale Chromium cells. The meaning of the decision changed: one post-canary step became two sequential tiers.
findings.implementation_impact: Built as written, 1.7.8 and 8.1 each boot twice after the canary (tier 1 Chromium, tier 2 Firefox) and CAP-7 almost never runs. That is the opposite of the wall-clock saving Budi chose.
findings.suggestion: Either collapse tiers 1+2 into one post-canary tier (other versions × Chromium∥Firefox, plus canary version × Firefox, one cold boot per version), or state explicitly that Budi approved the 3-tier split and accepts the double boot.

findings.location: SPEC.md Success signal ('A clean release gate boots each version at most once') vs tier-matrix.md tiers 0-2
findings.issue: In a clean run under the tier matrix, 9.1 boots warm (tier 0), then cold for the full tier-0 run, then again for Firefox in tier 2. 1.7.8 and 8.1 boot in tier 1 and again in tier 2. 'At most once' holds only if 'release gate' means tier 2 alone, and the doc never defines that scope.
findings.implementation_impact: The success signal cannot be checked: I can't tell which boots count, so I can't write a pass/fail check for it.
findings.suggestion: Define 'release gate' as a specific tier or tier set, and restate the boot-count criterion per version across the whole tiered run (e.g. 'each non-canary version boots once after tier 0').

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-1 / Constraints ('Tiering is internal to psm-validate') — no owner named
findings.issue: The doc never says whether the tiering is mechanised in a script (new flag on ps-run-layer.py? a new orchestrator script? ps-plan-layers emitting a tier plan?) or is prose in SKILL.md/run-phases.md that the model follows. CAP-1's success criterion ('no non-canary cell boots until the canary passes') can only be enforced and tested if a script owns it.
findings.implementation_impact: This is the core architecture decision, and I would have to guess it. Prose-only tiering gives no testable guarantee. A script needs CLI design (flag names, output schema), and none is given.
findings.suggestion: Name the owning script and its interface (e.g. ps-plan-layers.py emits `tier` and `next_tier_cells`, and ps-run-layer.py gets `--tier N`), or state explicitly that tiering is orchestrator prose and adjust CAP-1's success criterion to something testable.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md 'Phase' column / SKILL.md Fase 1-2 / run-phases.md
findings.issue: Tier 0 maps to Phase 1 and tier 2 to Phase 2, but tier 1 ('Fan-out') maps to neither. The doc does not say where Layers 2/5 (flashlight, scenario) for non-canary versions run, or when the Layer 3 adversarial lenses spawn (run-phases: 'at the start of Phase 2, after source stops being patched'). A tier-1/2 failure loops back to tier 0 and patches source again.
findings.implementation_impact: I can't update SKILL.md/run-phases.md consistently. Lenses could be spawned at tier 1 and then go stale after a loop-back. Flashlight/scenario per-version convergence (existing Phase 1 'finish one version before moving on') conflicts with 'only the canary in tier 0'.
findings.suggestion: State, per tier, which layers run for which versions (e.g. Phase 1 = tier 0 + tier 1 for all per-version layers; Phase 2 = tier 2 + Layer 3 + merge + aggregate). Also state that a loop-back re-enters Phase 1 and invalidates spawned lenses.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md Rules bullet 2 vs SPEC.md Open Questions #3 vs CAP-5
findings.issue: Rule 2 says a tier-1/2 failure for V returns the loop to tier 0 'with V as the cell being fixed', so tier 0 is no longer canary-only. In the same breath it asks whether the canary should switch to V, and the SPEC repeats that as an Open Question. CAP-5's warm container is defined only for 'the canary'. The doc also leaves open whether the cell being fixed is V×Chromium or V×Firefox when tier 2 failed on Firefox, and whether a warm container is used for V. After V is fixed, does the 9.1 canary have to pass again before tier 1 restarts, given that the patch staled all versions?
findings.implementation_impact: The loop-back path has no defined behaviour, and it is the path every real bug takes.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the open question. Define the loop-back cell as (V, failing browser), say whether the warm container applies to it, and give the re-promotion order after the fix (e.g. the fixed cell cold+full, then the canary, then tier 1).

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-5 / Constraints (Job ID ownership) vs ps-flashlight-run.py cleanup_decision / LABEL_OWNER_PID / job_register
findings.issue: Orphan detection is label-based: a container is removed by `--cleanup-orphans` when its `psm.owner-pid` process is dead. Each psm-validate invocation is a new process with a new Job ID (job_register, make_job_id; ps-run-layer makes one ID per invocation). A warm container that outlives iteration N's process is therefore 'owner-dead'. Any session's `--cleanup-orphans` will delete it between iterations, and iteration N+1 (new process, new Job ID) cannot own it. The doc doesn't name what owns the warm container between iterations.
findings.implementation_impact: I have to invent a lifetime model: a keeper daemon, a persistent job ID reused via `--job-id`, or new owner-label semantics. Each one changes stop-job/cleanup-orphans safety, which the constraints say must stay intact.
findings.suggestion: Specify the ownership model. For example, a detached keeper process registered under a stable warm Job ID owns the container (so it is 'owner-alive'), and fix-loop iterations attach via `--warm-job <id>`. Then define how `--stop-job` and `--cleanup-orphans` behave on it.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-5 — discovery, invalidation, teardown of the warm container
findings.issue: No flag or mechanism is given for an iteration to find and attach to the warm container: no state file, no label query, no port/ps_domain reuse. Nothing says when it must be discarded (tag-map/image bump, config change, container unhealthy, canary browser/version change). Nothing says who tears it down when tier 0 promotes; the matrix requires the last tier-0 run to be a cold boot.
findings.implementation_impact: Without these I would invent CLI flags and lifecycle rules. A forgotten warm container leaks a PS+DB pair on a shared WSL daemon that is already memory-starved.
findings.suggestion: Add the flag names (e.g. `--keep-warm` / `--use-warm <job>`) and the invalidation triggers. Add an explicit teardown step at promotion, and in headless mode at the end of the run.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-5 'DB reset to the post-boot baseline' and 'reinstalled module'
findings.issue: The baseline-capture mechanism is not specified. ps-scenario-run.py already has snapshot_db (taken AFTER install), but the doc neither points to it nor says whether the baseline is pre-install. 'Reinstalled module' is ambiguous: uninstall then install, or reset the DB then a fresh install? Filesystem state (copied module dir, overrides, var/cache, opcache) is not reset, so stale compiled classes/templates can make a warm run test old code.
findings.implementation_impact: The CAP-5 success criterion ('data from the previous iteration cannot cause a finding') can't be guaranteed or tested. A warm false-pass or false-fail is exactly what the convergence loop must not produce.
findings.suggestion: Specify: capture a DB snapshot after wait-healthy and before the first install (reuse ps-scenario-run snapshot_db). Each iteration restores the DB, removes `modules/<mod>` and clears var/cache (and opcache), then installs. Add a test that a row written in iteration N is absent in N+1.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-2 / CAP-4 / CAP-5 — evidence storage per (version, browser) vs ps-run-layer.py per_version_file / merge_versions_field
findings.issue: Per-version evidence is ONE file per version, `<module>-e2e-<ver>.json`. A tier-2 Firefox-only run for V would overwrite V's Chromium evidence from tier 1. A failed-only (CAP-4) or warm (CAP-5) run would overwrite full cold evidence. Freshness is judged by file mtime, so writing any cell refreshes the mtime of every cell in the file: stale Chromium evidence would read as fresh after a later Firefox run. The doc gives no storage shape for per-cell evidence.
findings.implementation_impact: Following the doc literally either loses evidence or makes stale cells look fresh. Both violate the honesty law.
findings.suggestion: Define the per-cell storage, e.g. `<module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.json`, or one file with per-browser entries each carrying its own `produced_at`/source fingerprint, `boot: cold|warm` and `scenario_set: full|partial`. Define how merge-only and the canonical file combine cells. Warm/partial evidence goes to a separate file that the gate never reads.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-2 'aggregate gives ready=false whenever any configured (version, browser) lacks fresh...' vs ps-aggregate.py main()
findings.issue: ps-aggregate.py has no `--browsers`/`--config` input and does no freshness check (the plan owns mtime freshness; ps-plan-layers docstring says aggregate 'cannot detect' stale files). It also cannot tell 'configured' from 'requested': the e2e file's `browsers` is the run's requested list, and a narrowed run records `['chromium']` as requested. merge_toplevel unions `browsers` across version files, so one version with Firefox hides another without it. The doc names none of these gaps or the fields to add.
findings.implementation_impact: I would have to choose whether aggregate imports plan freshness logic (it already loads ps-plan-layers as `pl`), how it learns the configured browser set, and which evidence fields mark cold/full. The CAP-2 test cannot be written until those exist.
findings.suggestion: Specify: aggregate takes `--config`/`--browsers` (configured set from psm_e2e_browsers) and reuses `pl` freshness per cell. It requires per-cell `boot=cold`, `scenario_set=full` and conclusive. It emits per-version per-browser cell status (e.g. `e2e_cells`) and drops ready if any cell is missing or stale.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-2 'the plan marks Firefox rerun' vs ps-plan-layers.py main()/per_version_rollup
findings.issue: ps-plan-layers.py has no `--browsers` argument. apply_config_file skips `psm_e2e_browsers` because the plan has no `browsers` dest (`hasattr` check). rerun_matrix entries are `{layer, version, per_version_capable}`, with no browser dimension. SKILL.md/run-phases.md tell the model that `all_reuse` is the gate. The doc doesn't define the new schema, i.e. how a browser shows up in the matrix and in `per_version[ver].rerun`.
findings.implementation_impact: A schema change in plan output silently breaks orchestrator prose and any consumer that reads `rerun` as a list of layer names.
findings.suggestion: Define the plan output change explicitly (e.g. `rerun_matrix` entries gain `browser` for layer e2e, and `per_version[ver].layers.e2e` becomes per-browser) and the `--browsers` flag/config mapping. Update run-phases.md accordingly.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-2 'configured (version, browser)' vs SKILL.md On Activation step 2 (operator may narrow browsers) and Non-goals
findings.issue: SKILL.md lets the operator narrow versions/browsers interactively ('tawarkan cakupan uji'). The doc doesn't say whether 'configured' means psm_e2e_browsers or the narrowed set chosen at activation. If it is the config, narrowing always yields ready=false and the menu option is pointless. If it is the narrowed set, the bankwire Chromium-only failure mode (brownfield) remains. The non-goal 'making Firefox optional for ready' suggests the config, but the existing `--require` escape hatch is also not addressed.
findings.implementation_impact: I can't decide what the aggregate compares against, or whether to change the activation menu text.
findings.suggestion: State: 'configured' = psm_e2e_browsers (and psm_target_versions). Interactive narrowing only shapes the current run, is recorded, and always drops ready. Say whether `--require` excluding e2e remains the only sanctioned way to gate without Firefox.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-3 'first conclusive blocking finding' vs ps-run-layer.py execute()/collect() and ps-e2e-run.py exit codes
findings.issue: Cells run as child processes per version. The parent only sees exit codes after a child finishes, and ps-e2e-run exits 1 both for blocking findings and for infra-inconclusive runs (pass stays False on errors). With the default `--jobs 3` and 3 versions, every child starts at once, so there are no 'unstarted cells' to stop. Inside a version, CAP-7 runs browsers in parallel, so there are none there either. The doc doesn't say at what granularity fail-fast acts or how 'conclusive blocking' is detected.
findings.implementation_impact: As specified, fail-fast saves nothing in tier 2. The 'wall-clock close to the failing cell's duration' criterion only holds with jobs=1 or sequential browsers. I would have to pick a detection method: parse child JSON, a new exit code, or a sentinel in the progress log.
findings.suggestion: Define the cell granularity fail-fast operates on and the signal it uses (e.g. a distinct child exit code for a conclusive blocking finding). Say whether in-flight siblings are left to finish (Assumption 2) even when that defeats the saving. Restate the success criterion with a concrete setup (e.g. `--jobs 1`, 3 versions, failure in the first).

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-3 'reported as not-run'
findings.issue: `not-run` is a new state with no defined home. ps-run-layer currently drops versions with no evidence from the canonical file, and aggregate reports them as 'versi tak ada di hasil e2e' (state skipped). The doc doesn't say whether not-run appears in the per-version file, the canonical file, the aggregate (which field and state value), or the headless return. It also doesn't say whether writing a not-run record overwrites previous evidence for that cell.
findings.implementation_impact: I must invent the schema. The test 'reported as not-run, never a pass' has no field to assert on.
findings.suggestion: Specify the field and value (e.g. per-cell `state: "not-run"`, `conclusive: false`, reason 'fail-fast after <cell>') in the layer JSON and the aggregate. Say that it never replaces existing cell evidence.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-4 failed-only rerun vs modules/bankwire/tests/e2e (order-dependent prerequisite scenarios)
findings.issue: Bankwire's scenarios depend on each other in order: checkout-with-bank needs bo-setup-country (activate Indonesia) and bo-setup-payment-country to have run first, and file-name order is load-bearing. Rerunning 'only the failed scenarios plus the universal smoke', especially after CAP-5's DB reset to baseline, skips the prerequisites and produces false failures or inconclusive results. The doc has no notion of scenario prerequisites.
findings.implementation_impact: The failed-only rerun would report spurious blocking findings on the very module named in the success signal.
findings.suggestion: Define how prerequisites are included: e.g. rerun the failed scenarios plus every scenario that sorts before them, or add a `requires`/`setup: true` field in the spec format. Note that writing new spec fields is distinct from the 'no new scenarios' non-goal.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-4 scenario identity and 'latest evidence'
findings.issue: The doc doesn't say what identifies 'a scenario that failed': spec `name` (e.g. `bankwire-bo-activate-indonesia`) or file stem (`bo-setup-country`). Findings carry `scenario` = name. It doesn't say whether failures are taken per (version, browser) or per version across browsers, or whether inconclusive scenarios count as failed. There is no flag name and no evidence field for 'partial'.
findings.implementation_impact: There are several plausible selection rules, and they give different rerun sets. The CLI and the partial marker would be invented.
findings.suggestion: Specify: selection key = spec `name` from `findings[].scenario` of the latest cell evidence for that (version, browser); inconclusive results do or do not count; the flag is, e.g., `--scenarios-from-failed`; evidence carries `scenario_set: "partial"` plus the list run.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-7 parallel browsers vs ps-e2e-run.py drive_engine (sync Playwright) and ps-run-layer.py execute() docstring
findings.issue: Engines are driven with `playwright.sync_api`. ps-run-layer's docstring relies on 'Playwright sync is not thread-safe, so it stays alone in its own process'. The doc doesn't say how concurrency is achieved (threads, each with its own sync_playwright; subprocesses; async API). It also doesn't say how two concurrent `browser:<engine>` phases are logged and timed.
findings.implementation_impact: This is an implementation choice with correctness risk (shared ctx dict, BO login of the same admin at the same time). I'd have to guess it.
findings.suggestion: Prescribe one model, e.g. one child process per engine against the same container, with per-engine ctx and progress lines tagged by engine. Note the concurrent same-admin BO login as acceptable or not.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-7 success ('Findings are identical to a sequential run') vs Open Question #1 and bankwire checkout-with-bank.json
findings.issue: Bankwire's checkout-with-bank spec explicitly relies on engines running in order: the second engine's add-bank POST is rejected as a duplicate, and checkout uses the first engine's row. bo-setup-country mutates global config. In parallel, both POSTs can race. Open Question #1 (serialize or declare isolation) is unresolved, yet CAP-7 asserts identical findings.
findings.implementation_impact: CAP-7 cannot be implemented to its done-criterion until the open question is answered. The identical-findings test would be flaky on bankwire.
findings.suggestion: Resolve OQ#1 before implementation (e.g. scenarios flagged `serial: true`, or all BO-mutating scenarios, run under a cross-engine lock). Restate the success criterion as 'identical findings on a module whose scenarios declare isolation'.

findings.location: SPEC.md Constraints 'one configurable cap' (concurrency)
findings.issue: The cap has no name, no config key, no default, and no unit. Does it count containers (versions), browser processes, or containers × browsers? How does it relate to the existing `--jobs` (default 3)? Does it replace `--jobs` or bound it? psm-setup's resolver/module.yaml has no such key.
findings.implementation_impact: I can't implement or test 'respects one cap' without picking all of these. Getting it wrong recreates the wait-healthy stalls the constraint exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Specify the key (e.g. `psm_e2e_max_parallel`), its unit (e.g. concurrent browser processes, each container counting as 1 plus its engines), its default, the precedence vs `--jobs`, and that it is added to psm-setup resolve-psm-config.py and module.yaml.

findings.location: SPEC.md Assumptions ('canary ... is configurable') / tier-matrix.md defaults
findings.issue: No config key or flag for the canary is defined, and the psm-setup resolver has none. The default is stated two ways: 'newest target (9.1)' and fixed '9.1'. These diverge when psm_target_versions changes or omits 9.1. The doc doesn't say what happens if the canary browser is not in psm_e2e_browsers.
findings.implementation_impact: I'd guess the key name and the default rule, and edge cases would crash or silently skip the canary.
findings.suggestion: Name the key(s) (e.g. `psm_e2e_canary=9.1:chromium`). Define the default as 'max(psm_target_versions) × first of psm_e2e_browsers', or fixed. Define the fallback when the canary is not in the configured set.

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-6 phase list vs ps-flashlight-run.py phases
findings.issue: CAP-6 lists only bring-up, wait-healthy, install and browser:<engine>. The real phases also include pull, wait-http, warmup-bo and teardown. In manual orchestrator mode the DB's wait-healthy runs nested INSIDE the bring-up phase (_bring_up_manual_inner calls wait_healthy), so the durations overlap. With CAP-7, browser phases overlap in time as well. The doc doesn't say where durations live in the layer JSON (per version entry vs top-level; a top-level dict would raise in merge_toplevel's scalar-conflict check) or which aggregate field surfaces them.
findings.implementation_impact: I'd guess the schema and whether nested/overlapping phases are subtracted, so the 'see whether boot or browser dominates' signal could be misleading.
findings.suggestion: Specify `versions[ver].phase_durations = {phase: seconds}` with all phases, a note that nested phases are not subtracted, a `wall_clock` total, and the aggregate field name (e.g. `e2e_phase_durations[ver]`).

findings.location: SPEC.md CAP-3 / CAP-7 success criteria ('close to', 'about the time of the slower engine')
findings.issue: Neither criterion gives a tolerance or a measurement method. Open Question #2 admits there is no wall-clock budget.
findings.implementation_impact: These criteria can't be turned into pass/fail tests.
findings.suggestion: Give testable forms, e.g. 'the run's wall-clock is at most the failing cell's duration + 10% + teardown', and 'the browser phase is at most max(engine) × 1.2 measured from CAP-6 durations'. Or mark them as observational, not acceptance criteria.

findings.location: SPEC.md Constraints (cold, full evidence) / Success signal test — evidence fields
findings.issue: The success-signal test asserts ready=false when a cell lacks 'fresh, full, cold-boot' evidence. No evidence field records boot mode (cold/warm) or scenario completeness (full/partial). ps-e2e-run's output has neither, and the plan's freshness check is mtime only.
findings.implementation_impact: The central honesty test has nothing to assert against until I invent these fields.
findings.suggestion: Name the fields and values (e.g. `boot: "cold"|"warm"`, `scenario_set: "full"|"partial"`, `scenarios_run: [...]`) and state that missing fields mean not gate-grade (as authored_assertions=None does today).

findings.location: SPEC.md Assumptions 'Tiering applies equally to ... headless' vs references/headless.md and caller skills
findings.issue: Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-scaffold, psm-optimize) run their own fix loop and call psm-validate repeatedly, and they are forbidden from running docker themselves. The doc doesn't say whether a warm canary persists across those separate headless invocations, who stops it at the end, or whether headless stops after tier 0 (returning blocked/ready=false) or always drives through tier 2. headless.md's return contract (`status`, `ready`, conclusiveness fields) gains nothing for tier or not-run.
findings.implementation_impact: The risk is leaked containers from headless runs and an unclear return value when only tier 0 ran.
findings.suggestion: Specify the headless behaviour: no warm container (or a mandatory teardown before returning), run tiers until the first failure, and return per-version ready plus a `tier_reached`/`not_run_cells` field. Update headless.md.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md tier 2 'plus any stale Chromium cell' vs per-version run-layer passthrough
findings.issue: ps-run-layer passes the same `--browsers` passthrough to every child. Tier 2 needs different browser lists per version (V1: firefox; V2: chromium+firefox). The doc doesn't say whether that means several run-layer invocations (several Job IDs, defeating the single cap) or a new per-version browser mapping.
findings.implementation_impact: This needs a CLI change to ps-run-layer that the doc doesn't describe.
findings.suggestion: Specify, e.g., `--cells 1.7.8:firefox,8.1:chromium+firefox` on ps-run-layer (one Job ID, one cap), or a plan-driven `--from-plan <plan.json>`.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md 'tier 0 clean' / 'tier 1 clean'
findings.issue: 'Clean' is undefined. It could mean E2E pass with zero blocking findings, all per-version layers for those versions passing, or ready-grade (conclusive, no inconclusive_note, not smoke-only). It could also include or exclude inconclusive infra results (e.g. a canary boot timeout).
findings.implementation_impact: The promotion gate is ambiguous. An infra-inconclusive canary could either block forever or promote unproven code.
findings.suggestion: Define clean = every cell in the tier has fresh, cold, full, conclusive passing E2E evidence with no inconclusive_note (equal to the per-cell ready rule). Say what to do on an inconclusive result (retry, or report and stop).

findings.location: brownfield.md 'bankwire run ... six aggregate reports across ~25 h'
findings.issue: The six bankwire aggregate stamps run from 20260908-072821Z to 20260909-010808Z, about 17.7 h, and the per-version e2e files end within that window. The ~25 h figure can't be verified from the files.
findings.implementation_impact: This is minor. The motivating baseline is overstated or comes from elsewhere, which matters if CAP-6 budgets are later set against it.
findings.suggestion: Correct it to about 18 h (stamps), or cite the source of the 25 h figure.

findings.location: brownfield.md 'ps-aggregate.py:919-923 records e2e_browsers (requested) vs e2e_browsers_run (available)'
findings.issue: Lines 922-923 are the code (919-921 are comments). More importantly, `e2e_browsers_run` comes from `browsers_available`, which is the binary-probe result, not the engines that actually drove (a launch failure still counts as 'available'). After a merge, both fields are unions across versions, so they cannot show per-version narrowing.
findings.implementation_impact: Anyone reusing these fields for CAP-2 would gate on the wrong data.
findings.suggestion: Note in brownfield that these fields are not per-cell truth. CAP-2 must use per-version `versions[ver].browsers` (engines actually driven) or the new per-cell evidence.

findings.location: SPEC.md frontmatter `sources: []` and preamble ('Source documents listed in frontmatter are for traceability')
findings.issue: The originating source (Budi's in-chat request and his scope answers) is not listed or quoted anywhere, so the scope decisions (tiered gate, warm container, timing, fail-fast + failed-only, Firefox parallel at the gate) cannot be traced. That is how the tier-1 restructuring drifted from 'then the other versions AND Firefox'.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer can't check intent when the matrix and the request disagree.
findings.suggestion: Add the verbatim request and Budi's answers as a source entry or an appendix.

findings.location: SPEC.md Non-goals ('Speeding up Layers ... 2, 5') vs Constraint 'one configurable cap' and the tier gating
findings.issue: Layers 2 and 5 also boot a PS+DB container per version and share the same daemon. The doc doesn't say whether the concurrency cap and tier gating apply to them, e.g. whether flashlight for 1.7.8 may run concurrently with the tier-0 E2E canary.
findings.implementation_impact: Running them concurrently would breach the cap's purpose (stalls at wait-healthy). Serialising them is a behaviour change the non-goals seem to exclude.
findings.suggestion: State whether the cap is global across all Docker layers or E2E-only, and whether Layers 2/5 follow the tier gating.

findings.location: SPEC.md (English) vs SKILL.md/run-phases.md (Indonesian) — document_output_language
findings.issue: The doc requires edits to SKILL.md and run-phases.md (Phase 1/2 refinement, new flags) but doesn't say what language to write them in. SKILL.md itself says artifacts follow `document_output_language`, and those files are Indonesian.
findings.implementation_impact: A minor guess, but mixed-language edits to the skill files would be a consistency defect.
findings.suggestion: State that edits to the skill files are written in the existing language of those files (Indonesian), and that machine tokens and field names stay in English.
